chunks: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masroor (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn al-Himyari, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Hashim, on the authority of al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt, said: I said to Ar-Rida (peace be upon him):
O son of God's Messenger, what do you say about the Qur'an?
He said: It is the Words of God. Do not go beyond it, and do not seek guidance in anything other than it, lest you go astray.

key_terms.الْقُرْآنِ: The Qur'an, the holy book of Islam
key_terms.تَضِلُّوا: You will go astray / be lost

ai.seo_question: What is the status of the Qur'an according to Imam Ar-Rida and how should one seek guidance?
ai.summary: In this tradition from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, Imam al-Rida (a.s.) establishes the Qur'an as the definitive, self-sufficient source of divine guidance, urging believers not to transcend its boundaries or seek truth in external sources. This affirmation underscores the Shia principle of the Qur'an's completeness and its role as the primary reference for understanding the Imams' teachings, preventing deviation into speculative or erroneous paths.
